meta.title_plain: How a game almost nobody played became a world hit
meta.teaser: Among Us flopped in 2018, then exploded two years later. Here's why.

page.title: How a game almost nobody played became a world hit
page.sub: The story of Among Us and Innersloth
page.bigIdea: Among Us had only a few dozen players for ages. A tiny team kept improving it anyway, and in 2020 the whole world joined in.

cards.title: A party game in space
cards.front: Where did the idea come from?
cards.back: Co-founder Marcus Bromander had played the party game Mafia since he was a kid. The team moved it to a spaceship and added tasks to do.
cards.tryit: Pick a game you know, like tag or hide and seek. In 10 minutes, invent one new twist for it.

cards.title: Only 30 to 50 players
cards.front: Launch day was not a party.
cards.back: Among Us came out on phones in June 2018. Only about 30 to 50 people played at once. Bromander said they were "really bad at marketing".
cards.tryit: Think of something you made that few people saw. Write one sentence on what you'd change.

cards.title: Keep going, keep updating
cards.back: The team nearly gave up several times. A small group of fans kept them going. They added online play, new tasks and two new maps in 2019.
cards.tryit: Choose one skill, like your tennis serve. Practise it for 10 minutes today, then again tomorrow.

cards.title: The 2020 explosion
cards.back: In 2020, big streamers on Twitch and YouTube started playing it. By September 2020, over 3.5 million people were playing at the same time.
cards.tryit: Ask two friends which game they found through a YouTuber. Did a video make them try it?

cards.title: Fix it, don't restart
cards.front: A sequel was planned. Then they stopped.
cards.back: In September 2020, Innersloth cancelled Among Us 2. They chose to rebuild and improve the original game, so players got new things faster.
cards.tryit: Take an old LEGO build and improve it in 15 minutes instead of starting a new one.

words.d: A game where you work out who's secretly on the other team.
Someone pretending to be something they are not.
A small game company that makes games on its own.
People playing a game at the very same moment.
A new version of a game that fixes or adds things.

quiz.hint: It's a game where some players are secretly on a hidden team.
quiz.why: Bromander loved Mafia as a kid and turned its secret-team idea into a space game.

quiz.q: Early on, only about 50 people played at once. In 2020, about 3.5 million did. About how many times bigger is that?
quiz.hint: Try dividing 3,500,000 by 50. Knock off zeros first to make it easier.
quiz.why: 3,500,000 ÷ 50 = 70,000, so the crowd grew about 70,000 times bigger.

quiz.q: What kept the team working when hardly anyone played?
opts: A small group of loyal fans
quiz.hint: Look back at the card about why they didn't quit.
quiz.why: A small but vocal player base gave them a reason to keep updating the game.

quiz.q: Why did Innersloth cancel Among Us 2?
opts: They wanted to improve the original faster
quiz.hint: Think about what players would get sooner: a whole new game or new stuff in the old one.
quiz.why: Rebuilding the original let millions of players get new features faster than waiting for a sequel.

page.think: Among Us got popular two years late. Is there something you're working on, like a serve or a Roblox game, that might just need more time?
